assessment.nobel_worthiness: Elucidation of GLP-1 as an incretin and its conversion into long-acting agonists has produced therapies with transformative, durable effects on type 2 diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal outcomes; originality is high and the physiological-to-clinical arc is unusually complete.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established GLP-1 physiology and actions; Mojsov contributed to identifying the bioactive peptide form. Knudsen's medicinal-chemistry role is important but is an industrial development contribution; a three-person physiology-centred configuration is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Large randomized trials and global clinical use give very strong independent confirmation; recognition is timely given the field's current impact.
uncertainties: Credit for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is disputed and I cannot verify the details independently.
Whether the prize should emphasize basic physiology or drug development (Knudsen) is unresolved; other early contributors may be missing from the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a transformative tool for causal, cell-type-specific control of activity, with enormous breadth and early clinical extensions in vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) plus neuronal implementation (Deisseroth, Boyden, Miesenboeck) form a compound discovery; a fair three-person split is hard and any selection omits important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for two decades and fully mature as a method; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: The line between microbial-opsin discovery and neuronal application is contested.
Several equally strong contributors would be excluded by the three-laureate limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells created a new class of living drugs, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies; the concept links immunology, gene engineering and clinical oncology.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain developed and clinically validated CAR designs including costimulation; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell therapy. Zelig Eshhar and others, not on the supplied list, are relevant to credit.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long follow-up confirm efficacy; limits in solid tumours and toxicity remain, but recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Foundational credit for the original chimeric receptor concept may lie outside the supplied names.
Durability and safety, including secondary malignancies, remain under study.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR and mTORC1/2 as central controllers of growth and nutrient sensing underpins understanding of metabolism, cancer, ageing and immunosuppression, with deep mechanistic clarity.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and defined its role; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and key pathway components. Schreiber's rapamycin chemistry is notable but more tool-oriented, so a two-person prize seems cleanest.
assessment.maturity: Findings are extensively confirmed across organisms; clinical translation (rapalogs, transplantation) is established though broader anti-ageing claims are unproven.
uncertainties: Contributions of Brown, Sabatini and Schreiber to mammalian TOR discovery involve overlapping credit.
Sabatini's later professional history may affect committee views, which I cannot assess.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating that TNF is a dominant driver of synovial inflammation and that its blockade treats rheumatoid arthritis changed care across many immune-mediated diseases and showed that targeting one cytokine can alter a chronic disease course.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini made the decisive translational link from mechanism to clinical proof; antibody engineering and other cytokine biology are adjacent contributions, so the pair is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use and independent confirmation in several diseases make this fully mature; the principle is long established.
uncertainties: As a rheumatologist I may be closer to this field; I weigh it using the same criteria as the others.
Other contributors to TNF biology and antibody drug development may be argued to be part of the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, with major implications for infection, autoimmunity, autoinflammation and cancer immunotherapy.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger; Barber identified STING. This is a clear mechanistic division, with other early STING and cGAS contributors beyond the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is robustly confirmed; clinical translation (STING agonists and antagonists) is still early, so the recognition could be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is not yet established.
Independent discovery of STING by several groups complicates attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BCL-2 family discoveries defined the control of apoptosis and enabled BH3-mimetic therapy such as venetoclax, linking basic cell-death biology to effective cancer treatment.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned BCL-2 and defined its family function with Strasser; Vaux showed BCL-2's survival role. The decisive credit includes earlier work on translocations by others, making allocation intricate.
assessment.maturity: Venetoclax approval and extensive confirmation make this mature; apoptosis was recognized in 2002, which lowers novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize on programmed cell death may reduce appetite for recognition.
Credit among Cory, Adams, Vaux and Strasser, and the earlier discovery of the translocation, is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib proved that inhibiting a causal oncogenic kinase can transform a lethal leukemia into a manageable disease, founding molecularly targeted oncology.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the drug discovery, Druker the clinical proof of concept, and Sawyers the resistance mechanism and second-line development; the trio is coherent, though Rowley and Nowell-Hungerford chromosome work and BCR-ABL cloning are upstream.
assessment.maturity: Long-term survival data are strong and mature; recognition has been long delayed in Nobel terms.
uncertainties: Chemistry credit for the compound inside the company may be split beyond Lydon.
Upstream discoverers of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL are not in the supplied names.
